A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PersonaCraft by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, inference timings, and a user study in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 reports original personalization and pose-generation experiments, component ablations, comparisons with fine-tuned baselines, and two user studies.

M1.justification: V1 combines depth-only SCNet with masked face-identity conditioning. V2 adds depth-and-normal SCNets, an occlusion-boundary network trained on masked depth edges, occlusion-dependent residual fusion, and spatially varying classifier-free guidance. It also introduces optional CLIP-derived body descriptions with regional prompting (Sections 3.1-3.3 and B.1).

E1.justification: Both versions use MPII-derived training data and COCO-WholeBody evaluation covering one to five people, alongside custom scenes, body-shape control, and stylization. Pose-guided generation was already tested in v1 Figure 9(a); v2 substantially expands its evaluation within the existing human-generation coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds pose-generation comparisons with T2IAdapter-SDXL, ControlNet-Flux, and HumanSD-SD2, and evaluates training-data-matched OMG variants and ControlNet-SDXL in Tables S8-S9. The personalization baseline families remain, but Textual Inversion and IPA-Face+OMG disappear from corresponding handshake and birthday qualitative panels (v1 Figure 4; v2 Figure 6).

E3.justification: Denoising steps change from 50 to 30, and the reported single-person:multi-person training ratio reverses from 1:2 to 2:1; the PDFs do not establish whether the latter reflects resampling or correction. V2 adds MPJPE, AP-0.5, IS/KID, and matched-training controls. The personalization study changes from 7 cases/123 participants to 15/103, and a pose study uses 15 cases/114 participants.

E4.justification: V2 adds depth/normal/RGB comparisons, OccNet and OccCFG ablations, spatial-guidance comparisons, conflicting body-composition examples, and a fitting-failure case (Table 5; Figures 9-11 and S22-S23). Body-parameter and conditioning-scale studies remain, while v1's explicit face-masking ablation in Figure 9(b) is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both present point estimates and preference percentages. Changed user-study sample sizes concern evaluation design, without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces overall face/body/CLIP scores of 0.305/0.531/0.252 with 0.317/0.560/0.273 under the revised method and settings, so these are not established same-setting gains. V2 adds pose, image-quality, component-ablation, and fine-tuned-baseline results; updates personalization preferences; and removes v1's cumulative Top-3 preference table.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions for ray-intersection-based occlusion masks and spatial guidance, and revises residual fusion (Equations 2-5). V1's explicit SMPLx vertex-shaping equation is omitted. These are limited changes to algorithmic formalization; neither version develops theorem/proof-based analysis, and the appendix identity and CLIP metric formulas remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add central contributions concerning fine-grained occlusion handling through OccNet and OccCFG, complementary depth/normal conditioning, and dual-pathway body representation. V1's broader full-body personalization and user-defined shape-control claims remain, but the claimed technical contribution substantially expands.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the effectiveness of depth conditioning for fine-grained occlusions and explains complementary depth/normal information, oversaturation from uniformly strong guidance, and SMPLx's difficulty representing muscle versus fat distribution. These substantive mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications extend v1's discussion, while dependence on face networks and fitting accuracy remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: V2 specifies Canny thresholds of 5/15, regional guidance scales of 3/5, conditioning weights of 0.8, and implementation details for CLIP-based body descriptions and regional prompting. Existing backbone, optimizer, hardware, and embedding details largely remain. V1's project-page access pointer is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around controllable human generation and spatial guidance, discussing HumanSD, Stable-Pose, HumanLDM, MIMO, StoryMaker, and ID-Patch. It additionally connects its new mechanisms to guidance-related prior work and MultiDiffusion, extending v1's emphasis on personalization and depth-based pose control.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into personalization and pose-controlled generation sections. Stylization, efficiency, and body-parameter analysis move into the supplement, and the bibliography now precedes a separately headed supplementary section.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the pipeline and training diagrams, restructures qualitative comparisons into horizontal grids with enlarged detail views, and adds component-analysis and failure-case figures. Table 1 changes from individual identity-count columns to Single/Multi/Total groups and adds pose/image-quality columns. Numerous figures and tables are added, resized, or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of pose and occlusion claims that v1 supported mainly qualitatively: direct pose metrics, component ablations, and matched-training comparisons in Tables 5 and S8-S9 make the advantages more assessable. Failure analysis also improves transparency. Reporting defects temper these gains: the lowest-KID claim contradicts Table 3 (HumanSD 0.082 versus PersonaCraft 0.091), and Table S6's body-shape total conflicts with Table 1. These defects do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support.
